content.comment_body: Good evening everyone. I am new to programming and just starting to learn. I'm using [product_name] and would like to ask a question to the experts here! The manual mentions that it is not possible to connect expansion modules with different voltage ratings, but I found an article on the website suggesting you can use this configuration with an [product_name] AM module. Is such a setup possible? [product_name] + [product_name] 12/24V DC + [product_name] 12/24R Thank you all in advance.

Hello [user_name], The [company_name] forum is split into two sections—one uses German, while the other (this one) operates in English for international discussions. You will receive responses in English here, so please try to post your questions in English as well. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, The manual also includes the relevant page, and it seems possible to me. However, I am not comfortable with using two different voltages in one system, as a minor mistake could result in hardware failure. Regards,
Hello [user_name], Thank you for your reply. My intention is to use the 12V module to enable 0-10V input on the 230V base system. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on whether it is feasible to combine [product_name] base modules at 230V with expansion modules operating at 12/24V. The manual appears to indicate this is not allowed, but website information suggests it may be supported with an appropriate module. Users highlight concerns about mixing voltages, warning about the risk of hardware damage and cautioning against such a configuration without clear official confirmation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks authoritative clarification about mixing expansion modules with different voltage specifications on a [product_name] system—ideally referencing official documentation or direct support from [company_name].
